output.summary: KEP-1635 requires k8s.io REST APIs to leave beta within nine months (three releases): either reach GA, or introduce a new beta and deprecate the previous one. Otherwise the beta API is deprecated with an announced intent to remove it. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale: Beta REST APIs are on by default, so users and vendors build on them, and there is little incentive to stabilize them, leaving some "perma-beta" APIs (CSRs, Ingresses) in beta for years. The policy sets a fixed deadline so each beta either graduates, gets a new beta version, or is deprecated. The implementation was reported as done in 1.19 and unchanged since, with the automatic removal making enforcement easier.

alternatives.why_not: Reviewers argued it was too aggressive; timothysc said "6 months seems a bit aggressive" and tallclair and others favored 9-12 months, so the window was extended to nine months.

alternatives.option: Limit the number of beta APIs a SIG can have at once
alternatives.why_not: Proposed by johngmyers as an alternative; liggitt replied it is "complementary to this proposal rather than an alternative to it", so it was not adopted as a replacement.

alternatives.option: Also cover alpha features and new fields in GA APIs
alternatives.why_not: Deferred. liggitt said "lifecycle policies around alpha and field-level changes can be follow-ups", and derekwaynecarr said alpha "can be evaluated separate from this enhancement".

alternatives.option: Enforce via tooling before adopting the policy
alternatives.why_not: deads2k said "We're agreeing to a policy here and will build enforcement as a post-step."

evidence.quote: This must happen within nine months (three releases). If it does not, the REST API will be deprecated with an announced intent to remove the API
6 months seems a bit aggressive. Folks come and go on the project and priorities change, 9-12 seems fair.
This was implemented back in 1.19 and has not changed since. The automatic removal made it slightly easier to enforce, the policy is the same.
We're agreeing to a policy here and will build enforcement as a post-step.
I agree lifecycle policies around alpha and field-level changes can be follow-ups.
